name: IEC BCD-to-seven-segment decoder
summary: IEC coder marked BCD/7SEG converting a 4-bit BCD input into seven segment-drive outputs a to g.
description: The BCD-to-seven-segment decoder is an X/Y coder with the qualifier BCD/7SEG, sometimes written BCD/7-SEG. Inputs are weighted 1, 2, 4 and 8 and outputs are labelled a to g for the display segments. Many devices add lamp test and blanking inputs shown with their own labels.

Seven-segment decoders appear on drawings for local numeric displays, counters and older instrument panels. The output stage type matters: many drivers have open-collector outputs intended to sink LED or lamp current, which should be shown with the open-circuit qualifier.
The symbol does not state segment current, display type (common anode or cathode) or how non-BCD codes are displayed. Those come from the device data and display selection.
readingNotes: Outputs a to g map to display segments.
Check output type and display common connection.
drawingChecklist: Label segment outputs a to g.
Show lamp test and blanking inputs where used.
Show current-limiting resistors and display wiring.
distinction: A BIN/OCT decoder activates one output per code; this coder activates a pattern of segments.
